title: Good-Faith Repayment Points in Waiver Decisions — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Training Bulletin
content:
Points are added to the waiver share on Benefit Overpayment Accounts for a claimant who repaid in good faith, counting the repayments received on the overpayment less those returned unpaid.

| Repayments received less those returned unpaid | Points added to the waiver share |
|---|---|
| Above zero and at least the plan's monthly installment | 0.05, the full good-faith points |
| Above zero but below the plan's monthly installment | 0.025, the part good-faith points |
| No repayment (zero or less) | None |

## Questions answered

**Which repayments are counted?** Every repayment received on the overpayment over its life, less every repayment on it returned unpaid by the bank. Benefit offsets and tax refund intercepts are not repayments.

**Which installment is compared?** The plan's monthly installment as shown on the overpayment record. Where the overpayment record shows a monthly installment of 0.00, any amount above zero is at least that installment.

**Worked figures (hypothetical).** Repayments of USD 100.00 and USD 100.00 were received and one was returned, leaving USD 100.00. Against a monthly installment of USD 80.00 the full points of 0.05 are added; against a monthly installment of USD 120.00 the part points of 0.025 are added. If both repayments had been returned, no points would be added.
